extracted.intended_audience: state and federal agency staff, municipal planners, community organizers, environmental justice advocates, and practitioners developing public participation plans
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, implementing, and evaluating public participation programs in environmental justice contexts, including legal compliance (Title VI), state examples, and practical plan elements to ensure meaningful community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of Public Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation (citizen participation/public involvement) describes the process of including the public in decision-making and activities to reach project goals; those affected by a decision have a right to be involved and contributed decisions should influence outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties include communities, individuals, companies, governments, institutions, or other stakeholders. Activities under this principle include seeking comments on issues and policies, sharing government information, and using public inputs in decision-making. Public participation processes should empower stakeholders to be involved in various aspects and degrees of decision-making and should facilitate the involvement of those impacted by a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Engagement Definition (NIH quote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Community engagement is “the process of working collaboratively with and through groups of people affiliated by geographic proximity, special interest, or similar situations to address issues affecting the wellbeing of those people.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this framing to center affected communities' geographic or situational affiliation when designing participation activities and to justify collaborative and capacity-building approaches in plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum of Community Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum of community engagement categorizes stances toward participation as: ignore, inform, consult, involve, collaborate, and defer to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spectrum provides a framework and shared language to communicate how much impact public participation will have, the community engagement goal, and the resource allocation ratio. Plans should identify where activities fall on the spectrum and be explicit about the expected degree of influence; the document notes that this is often not communicated to community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Public Participation Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical activities include seeking comments on issues and policies, sharing government information, implementing educational and public awareness programs, and using public inputs in decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that fit the chosen place on the engagement spectrum; combine information-sharing, consultation, and participatory processes as needed. Examples: public notices, comment periods, community meetings, outreach campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empowerment and Meaningful Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation processes should empower stakeholders and promote meaningful involvement rather than symbolic or minimal engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful participation implies that contributions can influence outcomes. Plans should include strategies to ensure marginalized communities have the capacity and opportunity to participate (e.g., accessible materials, translation, scheduling, facilitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan public participation activities for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A public participation program must strategically plan activities to assist responsible parties, municipalities, applicants, and contractors in planning, facilitating, and implementing communicative strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning entails selecting appropriate engagement methods, timing, responsible parties, resources, and metrics for success—tailored to project stage and affected populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct public participation to promote meaningful participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out public participation activities in ways that actively promote meaningful participation by citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outreach techniques that lower participation barriers (e.g., accessible venues, multiple meeting formats, proactive outreach). Ensure facilitators are trained to solicit input and incorporate diverse perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate results of public participation into decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation programs must incorporate the results of public participation into decision-making as appropriate and provide opportunities for ongoing communication before final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish procedures to document public input, demonstrate how input influenced decisions (or explain why it did not), and communicate back to participants to close the feedback loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and adjust public participation activities for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate public participation activities for effectiveness and adjust the program as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build monitoring and evaluation into the plan (e.g., participation metrics, representativeness, satisfaction), use findings to refine methods, and report evaluation results to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin early and apply requirements consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation programs must begin early in the project lifecycle, and participation requirements must be applied consistently from step to step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement increases opportunity for meaningful input; consistent application avoids procedural gaps that undermine trust and legal compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with staff, agencies, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties should coordinate with staff, agencies, and the public to plan and implement participation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate roles and responsibilities across agencies and stakeholders, align timelines and messaging, and use coordination to avoid confusion and duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title VI compliance requirements for federal funding recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of federal funding (e.g., from EPA) must comply with Title VI implementing regulations and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum requirements include: (a) collect, maintain, and provide information showing compliance with Title VI and the regulations; (b) designate a nondiscrimination compliance coordinator; (c) adopt grievance procedures assuring prompt and fair resolution of discrimination complaints; and (d) provide continuing and prominent public notice of nondiscrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, or disability and identify the nondiscrimination coordinator. Plans for publicly funded programs must reflect these obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State public participation plans and codified EJ definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: States should develop public participation plans and may codify an environmental justice definition that clarifies fair treatment and inclusion in environmental decisionmaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: California’s statutory EJ definition and CEQA requirements to inform decisionmakers and the public about potential environmental impacts and to provide opportunities for public review and participation. Compare state practices (e.g., CA, NY, MI) to identify stronger models and gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and language access / accessibility services
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation should include translation, transcription, and interpreting services and other accessibility accommodations as needed (e.g., large print, braille, audio recordings, qualified language and ASL interpreters, document translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contact information and processes for obtaining translation services are provided; address language access proactively to avoid Title VI violations and to enable meaningful participation from non-English speakers and people with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to information and educational outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide public access to information, and implement educational and public awareness programs to enable informed participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make technical information understandable, provide summaries and context, offer training or informational sessions, and maintain web/online information to support ongoing engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about level of engagement and resource allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and communicate where engagement activities fall on the spectrum of engagement and the expected community impact and resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being explicit about whether a process is informational only, consultative, or collaborative helps set expectations and builds trust. Include estimated resources, timelines, and what authority public input will have.
